# 1 Clement 56 — Disagreement Log
**Chapter:** 1 Clement 56 (16 verses)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA
**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Total disagreements logged:** 5

---

## V.1 — "commemoration" / "remembrance"
- **EMET:** "commemoration" / **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** "remembrance"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Commemoration" (EMET) — the Greek *mneia* in this context likely refers to the liturgical commemoration of the faithful before God. The term evokes eucharistic memory more than mere "remembrance."

---

## V.4 — "chastens" / "disciplines"
- **EMET:** "chastens" / **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** "disciplines"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Disciplines" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) — though "chastens" is traditional, "disciplines" better renders *paideuei* as the formative education of a child, not merely punishment.

---

## V.4 — "scourges" / "chastises"
- **EMET:** "scourges every son" / **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** "chastises every son"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Scourges" (EMET) — the Greek *mastigoi* means literally to whip/flog. The physical imagery of Proverbs 3 and Hebrews 12 should be preserved. "Chastises" softens it.

---

## V.10 — "lash of the tongue" / "scourge of the tongue" / "slanderous tongues"
- **EMET:** "lash of the tongue" / **LOGOS:** "scourge of the tongue" / **PNEUMA:** "slanderous tongues"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Scourge of the tongue" (LOGOS) — maintains the physical "whip" metaphor (*mastixi glōssēs*) while creating a deliberate verbal echo of v.4's "scourges." PNEUMA loses both the metaphor and the echo.

---

## V.15 — "tomb" / "grave"
- **EMET:** "enter the tomb" / **LOGOS:** "come to the grave" / **PNEUMA:** "go to your grave"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Come to the grave" (LOGOS) — the Greek *taphos* means burial place/grave. "Tomb" (EMET) implies a specific structure; "grave" is the broader and more natural English rendering here.

---

*— SOPHIA*
